description: Migration creates `calendars` table (personal/group, owner_user_id, name, description, color, is_archived, created_by, timestamps) with PK (tenant, calendar_id), partial unique personal-per-user index, type check constraints, Citus distribution by tenant.

Migration creates `calendar_shares` table (calendar_id, grantee_type user|team, grantee_id, access_level free_busy|read|edit|manage) with unique (tenant, calendar_id, grantee_type, grantee_id), cascade FK to calendars, Citus distribution.
Migration adds nullable `schedule_entries.calendar_id` with composite FK to calendars and (tenant, calendar_id) index.
Register `calendars` and `calendar_shares` in packages/db tenantTableMetadata and the migration shim registry (server/migrations/utils/tenantDb.cjs).
Add ICalendar, ICalendarShare, CalendarAccessLevel types and extend IScheduleEntry with calendar_id, access ('full'|'busy'), can_edit.

calendarAccess.resolveCalendarAccess(viewer) returns visible personal-calendar user ids with effective level, visible group calendars with level, and canViewAll, in a bounded number of queries (direct shares + team shares + group calendars).
Effective level is the max of direct user grants and grants to any team the viewer belongs to; team membership is resolved at read time.
Shares granted by or to inactive users are ignored during access resolution.
`user_schedule:update` holders resolve as edit on every internal user's personal calendar and manage on every group calendar (preserves current behavior).

calendarAccess.evaluateEntryAccess(entry, access) returns full/busy/none and canEdit per the ordered PRD visibility and modify rules (assignee, group calendar level, best assignee personal level, private masking).
maskEntry strips title (→ translated Busy), notes, work item, and assignee details server-side for busy entries.
ScheduleEntry.getAll accepts an optional visibility filter (userIds, calendarIds, includeUnassignedAppointmentRequests) applied in SQL before recurrence expansion.
Recurring virtual instances inherit calendar_id and are evaluated/masked identically to their parent.

getScheduleEntries uses the resolver: returns only visible entries (own, shared personal, group calendars), masked where busy, annotated with access and can_edit; honours requested user/calendar overlays.
getScheduleEntryById enforces user_schedule:read and the resolver (returns not-found for none, masked for busy).
addScheduleEntry allows creating entries for users the viewer has edit on, and on group calendars where the viewer has edit+; rejects otherwise.

updateScheduleEntry/deleteScheduleEntry allow changes when the viewer is an assignee, has edit on any assignee's personal calendar, edit+ on the entry's group calendar, or user_schedule:update; private entries remain sole-assignee only.
Assignee changes by non-admins are restricted to users the viewer has edit on plus themselves (server-enforced).
Server rejects/clears is_private when calendar_id is set; calendar_id may only reference a non-archived group calendar the viewer can edit.

getMyCalendarShares / setMyCalendarShares: owner lists and upserts/removes shares on their personal calendar (lazy personal calendar creation, no self-share, internal-user grantees only, free_busy/read/edit only).
user_schedule:update holders can view and change shares on any user's personal calendar.

getCalendarsVisibleToMe returns My calendar, People (visible personal calendars with level and deterministic color) and Group calendars (with level, color, archived only for managers) plus viewer capabilities.
createGroupCalendar creates a group calendar with name, color, description and initial members; creator is added as manage.
updateGroupCalendar and setGroupCalendarShares (manage/admin only) rename/recolor/describe and upsert/remove member shares; reject removing or downgrading the last manager.
archiveGroupCalendar / restoreGroupCalendar (manage/admin only); archived calendars and their entries are excluded from non-manager views.
User deletion and team deletion paths remove calendar_shares where the deleted user/team is the grantee.
Add CALENDAR_SHARE_GRANTED event schema and publish it when a user grantee is newly added or their level changes.
internalNotificationSubscriber creates an internal notification for user grantees on CALENDAR_SHARE_GRANTED; migration seeds the notification template.
REST GET /api/v1/schedules (list and by id) uses the resolver instead of canViewAllSchedules.
Replace client-side `user_schedule:read:all` checks (useScheduleViewer, ScheduleCalendar) with server-provided capabilities.
Schedule sidebar gains a Calendars section: My calendar, People, Group calendars, with visibility checkboxes and color swatches; People lists only calendars the viewer can see.
Overlay selection (people + group calendars) persists in user_preferences and restores on load, dropping calendars that are no longer visible.
Focus can be set to self or any calendar the viewer has edit on; new entries default the assignee to the focused owner.
Overlay entries render with their calendar color stripe; busy entries render as 'Busy' blocks.
Drag/resize enabled for any entry with can_edit (not only the focused user's).
Opening a busy entry shows a read-only popup with time and 'Busy' only.
Share my calendar dialog (Schedule page + Profile > Calendar settings): list current shares, add users/teams via UserAndTeamPicker with level, change level, remove.
New/Manage group calendar dialogs: name, color (ColorPicker), description, member list with levels, archive/restore.

EntryPopup: Calendar field (Personal or editable group calendars); hides Private toggle when a group calendar is selected; assignee picker limited to editable users for non-admins; assignees optional on group entries.
Empty-state calls to action in People and Group calendars groups.
All new UI strings added to msp/schedule namespace for every supported locale.
